analyst_view.overall: Cagliari (11th, 16 points, LLLWL, 2-0 loser at Como) host AC Milan (4th, 27 points, three straight league wins, 5-1 against Frosinone) on Monday evening; the numbers make Milan clear favourites. Ruben Amorim's Milan lose Luka Modric to a thigh strain (counted by the numbers), with Jashari expected to replace him, and also miss Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek and Chukwueze; one unconfirmed report adds Pavlovic, and they played at Olympiacos in the Europa League on Thursday. Fabio Pisacane's Cagliari miss Liteta, Mina, Winks and Felici, while Mendy and Adopo did partial training and are closer to returning (one report); the numbers take Mendy out. Referee Marco Di Bello is one of the lowest-card referees (2.8 a game), which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, 0.9 for Cagliari, already taking about 12% off Cagliari for Mendy and a little off Milan for Modric, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze. One report says Mendy is close to returning after partial training, which would give some of that back, so I lean a touch higher (+2%), about 2.55; nothing is confirmed yet.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, already cutting Milan for only 10 corners in their last six; Amorim's side have struggled to push opponents back. Cagliari usually defend compactly at home and the two previews disagree on their shape (4-4-2 or 3-5-2), so nothing points clearly either way; I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards, already cut about 24% for referee Marco Di Bello (2.8 cards a game) and trimmed for Milan's recent record. Cisse is on a caution but not banned, and this is no derby, so I stay at about 2.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots, raised for Cagliari's recent volume and cut 8% for Milan's low recent shooting (60 in six). Milan's Thursday trip to Olympiacos and Modric's absence could slow them, but they won their last three league games and Jashari is a like-for-like option, so I stay at about 24.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target, already lifted a little because Milan have allowed 34 on target in their last six and Cagliari 38. Milan's striker Goncalo Ramos is named in the probable XI despite recent knocks, and Cagliari's Nzola and Maldini lead their line as usual, so I stay at about 9.
